paragraphs: Caution signal | This page covers U.S. 13-1075.00, handling labor disputes, collective agreements, and grievances. Labor relations specialists may represent management or employees under authorization, or undertake mediation and coordination; first state identity and authority, check facts objectively, disclose conflicts, and follow applicable procedures, without treating all one-party representation or lawful one-sided communication as misconduct. Risks concern records, confidentiality, procedural deadlines, terms, and authority. O*NET exact occupation 2024 employment 65,400 → 2034 employment 65,400, 2024—2034 growth 0%, average annual openings 5,100 including replacement; all retain the old period. 2025 median annual wage is 95,420 USD; insufficient evidence: exact Chinese occupational wages were not established.

Responsibility assessment | Fact investigation, interpretation of terms, and recommendations may be job duties within applicable law and authority; refer matters requiring a lawyer, arbitration, or final commitment authority according to roles. Representing one side still requires accurate records and no fabricated grounds; X's four work samples test these distinctions.

Assessing fit | Use X's fixed three records and v2 agreement to check 1/3 hour discrepancies, the provisional 5×10=50 calculation, the day 5 deadline and day 6 lateness, and lack of authority to guarantee 80; submit four work samples: fact table, version and deadline checks, draft response, and authority items requiring verification. The task, answer, and seven-day plan of 20—30 minutes daily appear in the pathway; use no real confidential information or simulated rules as law.

Fit signals | O*NET 13-1075.00 work activities emphasize obtaining information, resolving conflicts and negotiating, communicating inside and outside the organization, making decisions and solving problems, and establishing and maintaining relationships. If you are willing to keep checking facts, contractual terms, and procedures, maintain procedural discipline and restraint amid conflict and multiple positions, and turn handling and negotiations into reviewable records, these daily demands are closer to your working style; interest and personality tools only help design trials, not determine hiring eligibility or performance.

Labor relations specialists handle grievances, collective agreements, and negotiations, checking facts, terms, and deadlines and keeping records. They may be authorized to represent management or employees; mediation roles require separate checks. U.S. 2025 median annual wage is 95,420 USD; insufficient evidence: exact Chinese occupational wages were not established.

entries: Work objects | Employee grievances and disputes, employment contracts and collective agreements, labor laws and procedural rules, and union and management demands form the basis of labor relations work within authorization and compliance boundaries.

Checkable outputs | Reviewable grievance intake and investigation records, contract and agreement term analyses, negotiation and mediation points and records, agreement or handling-decision explanations, and external communication records; results must be traceable to factual materials and agreement or legal grounds.

Complete workflow | Receive and verify facts → check contract and agreement terms → identify applicable law and procedural deadlines → develop handling or negotiation plans → record, explain, and communicate with relevant parties.

paragraphs: Key judgments | O*NET work context reports: email, 95% daily; telephone conversations, 79% daily; face-to-face discussions, 63% daily; constant contact with others, 62%; conflict situations, 43% daily; decision impact, 71% important results; time pressure, 48% at least weekly but not daily. Judgments rely on factual materials and agreement terms, applicable law and procedural deadlines, and confidentiality and authorization boundaries. These are U.S. O*NET respondent distributions, not fixed conditions for China or each individual.

Environment and pace | Work mainly involves communication, desk analysis, and coordination: controlled indoor environment, 63% daily; sitting, 62% more than half the time; decision freedom, 43% some freedom; task priorities and goals, 55% some freedom; workweek, 52% over 40 hours; written letters, 37% at least weekly but not daily; exactness or accuracy, 38% very important; dealing with unpleasant or angry people, 37% at least weekly but not daily; competition, 60% moderate. Grievance and negotiation cycles drive the pace. These are U.S. O*NET respondent distributions, not fixed conditions for China or each individual.

Research inputs | Retain official summary interest code ECS; detail E78/C60/S45 gives intensities, not a basis for inventing another official code. Job Zone4 general preparation does not mean uniform service requirements; no Bright Outlook designation. Other services (except public administration) at 77% in 2025 is an industry distribution. 2025 U.S. annual wage 10/25/50/75/90 percentiles are 50,490, 71,920, 95,420, 123,420, and 156,180 USD; official hourly wages are 24.27, 34.58, 45.87, 59.34, and 75.09 USD, respectively. Exact U.S. 13-1075 employment moves from 66,300 in 2025 → 67,700 in 2035, with 2025—2035 growth of 2% and average annual openings of 4,800 including growth and replacement; net growth of 1,400 is not average annual openings. Overall employment projections are not AI attribution. Exact Chinese wages were not established and cannot be filled with industry proxies.

This work first checks objects (employee grievances and disputes, employment contracts and collective agreements, labor laws and procedural rules), inputs (factual materials and witness statements, contract and agreement terms, applicable law and deadlines, authorization and confidentiality requirements), and deliverables (grievance intake and investigation records, term analyses, negotiation and mediation records, agreement or handling explanations). Anything unverified remains pending verification; positions or intuition cannot replace factual and agreement grounds.

Work cycle | Check facts, agreement versions, and deadlines → state representative identity and authority → investigate, analyze, and draft or negotiate → review, record, and escalate. Pause affected conclusions or commitments when uncertain while continuing permitted investigations and procedural deadline management; legal recommendations may fall within the role, while final rulings, litigation representation, or payments require separate authority checks.

Adjacent-duty boundaries | This page covers only the exact O*NET-SOC 13-1075.00 occupation, Labor Relations Specialists. Adjacent occupations such as chief executives, public relations managers, administrative services managers, compensation and benefits managers, and human resources managers differ in work objects, decision level, authority, and responsibility boundaries. They are not interchangeable based solely on titles, and proxy descriptions cannot replace legal authorization, collective agreements, and organizational requirements.

Chief executives | Core outputs are overall organizational strategy and operating results. This occupation mainly involves dispute handling and agreement negotiations; decision levels and entrusted duties differ, so titles alone do not make them interchangeable.

Public relations managers | Core outputs are external image and communications. This occupation mainly involves factual investigations, agreement interpretation, and negotiations; external messaging and those owed responsibility differ and require separate checks.

Administrative services managers | U.S. 11-3012.00 manages office support services such as records, information, and mail distribution; do not import all facilities manager 11-3013 duties. This occupation focuses on labor disputes and agreements; administrative operations management scope and authority require additional evidence.

Compensation and benefits managers | Core outputs are compensation and benefits design and governance. This occupation focuses on disputes, negotiation, and agreement implementation; plan design and negotiating representation are different roles requiring separate checks.
Labor relations specialists' work objects and AI boundaries: which steps may receive assistance and which judgments must remain human responsibilities.

AI may assist research, summaries, and drafts using approved fictional materials, but outputs must be checked against original records, term versions, and deadlines; widespread occupational adoption, efficiency gains, or replacement probabilities have not been established. Authorized people remain responsible for negotiation identity, handling decisions, and commitments.

Evidence note | ILO2025 global exposure research does not measure labor relations specialist adoption, losses, or efficiency gains; NIST's generative AI risk framework supports preventing fabrication, privacy risks, and human verification. Current unique U.S. recruitment mentions in 2025 are Office23%, Excel17%, PowerPoint12%, Outlook8%, Workday/ServiceNow at 6% each, Word4%, and PeopleSoft/SharePoint/Access at 1% each; Kubernetes has no listed percentage, which does not mean 0. Software mentions do not equal AI adoption or necessity. The original internal scale is only an editorial framework and grants no legal or negotiation authority.

Differences | Assistance trials can be designed for text tasks, but textual form does not automatically prove acceleration; X checks three-record discrepancies, v1/v2 miscitation, and the unauthorized commitment of 80, retaining revisions.

Responsibility chain | From confirming facts and authorization through tool processing, human review, handling or negotiation decisions, records, and external communication, each step needs an identified responsible person and traceable evidence; unverified generated content must not directly become handling grounds or external commitments.
Tool use | First establish X's human baseline for facts, versions, and deadlines, then compare errors and time in approved tool drafts; without actual measurement, do not claim changed efficiency.

Potential assistance: case and term research, material organization and summaries, negotiation material drafts, and draft records; results can be checked afterward but still require review against original contracts and agreements, applicable law, and procedural deadlines.

Human control points: check original contracts and agreements, applicable law, and factual materials, taking responsibility for factual findings, agreement and legal interpretation, handling and negotiating positions, and external communication.

Occupational title comparison | This page corresponds to U.S. O*NET-SOC 13-1075.00 Labor Relations Specialists. This round did not establish single-occupation wages in Chinese public statistics corresponding to this exact occupation; the National Bureau of Statistics publishes average annual urban unit employee wages by industry section. Industry averages cannot be presented as national occupational medians, and Chinese page language establishes no equivalent Chinese occupation or wage mapping.

Occupational scope and industry proxy | This page's Chinese conclusions are limited to mainland China and the current statistical scope. As a checkable proxy with a different scope, National Bureau of Statistics 2025 average annual wages of urban unit employees show leasing and business services industry section averages of 110,162 yuan/year for urban nonprivate units and 68,919 yuan/year for urban private units; these cover multiple occupations and exclude individual businesses, and cannot be described as labor relations specialists' national medians, percentiles, or starting pay. Competent authorities, industries, and employers set qualifications and training for related Chinese jobs, requiring separate checks.

Insufficient evidence: this round did not establish a nationwide occupational wage distribution in mainland China exactly corresponding to O*NET 13-1075.00 Labor Relations Specialists; industry section averages such as leasing and business services cannot generate occupational national medians, percentiles, or starting pay. This page uses no industry proxies, recruitment quotes, or U.S. data to fill occupational values.
AI and pay | No causal data on occupational AI adoption, efficiency gains, and income was established; exposure or software mentions cannot predict pay rises, cuts, or unchanged compensation.

2025 U.S. annual wage 10/25/50/75/90 percentiles are 50,490, 71,920, 95,420, 123,420, and 156,180 USD; hourly median is 45.87 USD. Exact U.S. 13-1075 employment moves from 66,300 in 2025 → 67,700 in 2035, with 2025—2035 growth of 2% and average annual openings of 4,800 including growth and replacement; net growth of 1,400 is not average annual openings. Overall employment projections are not AI attribution. O*NET other services (except public administration) accounts for 77% of 2025 employment, an industry distribution.

OEWS covers employer-reported wages, including incentive pay but excluding overtime pay, nonproduction bonuses, and employer-paid benefits; percentiles are not starting pay, after-tax income, or individual quotes. Hourly wages are disclosed separately by the source.

Interpretation | This scope helps explain the occupation's wage distribution and demand direction, but is not an individual quote and cannot be compared directly with mainland China or any other market; a projection of 'little or no change' does not mean individual employment stability or guarantee employment.

Industry scope | Retain other services (except public administration) at 77% in 2025 as an employment industry distribution, not wages. BLS2025 industry annual wage medians: management of companies 99,260, labor organizations such as unions 94,850, government (excluding state and local education and hospitals) 91,050 USD. Union employment share of 72% in 2025 and O*NET2025 other services at 77% use different classification levels.

Influencing factors | Industry and employer type (business, government, union, or association), negotiating representative duties, region, and collective agreement terms affect actual income and stability; this page's percentiles are statistical positions, not specific organizations or jobs.

Which interests, abilities, and working styles matter more for labor relations specialists? This page discusses fit through work samples and responsibility boundaries only, without using personality labels to replace hiring eligibility or performance judgments.

Direct answer | Fit signals are willingness to keep checking facts, contractual terms, and procedures, procedural discipline and restraint amid conflict and multiple positions, reviewable handling and negotiation records, and seeking instructions when facts are uncertain or authority is exceeded, rather than personality labels. Interest and personality tools only help design trials, not determine hiring eligibility or performance.

Positive signals | You can receive and investigate grievances through procedures and check contract and agreement terms; identify deadlines and confidentiality requirements and clearly document key points; and preserve investigation, negotiation, and communication processes as reviewable records.

Caution conditions | Risk signals include insufficient factual investigation evidence, incorrect agreement or legal interpretation, missed grievance or arbitration deadlines, employee or negotiation information leaks, unclear representative identity, undisclosed conflicts, or commitments beyond authority; difficulty with conflict and multiple parties' pressure represents practical costs to weigh seriously.

Trial action | Use X's fixed materials to check 1/3 hour discrepancies, v2's provisional 50 calculation, the day 5 deadline, and day 6 lateness; do not promise 80. Submit four work samples: fact table, version and deadline checks, draft response, and authority items requiring verification; follow the seven-day plan.

Conclusion | Activity preferences are closer to an Enterprising, Conventional, and Social combination (O*NET interest code ECS); interest codes only help design trials, not determine hiring eligibility or performance.

Personality boundaries | This page has not verified scale predictive validity for occupational performance; use X investigation, term versions, deadlines, and communication revisions to ask questions, without inferring performance or hiring from personality labels.

Conclusion | RIASEC or personality frameworks only help formulate questions; they cannot replace occupational qualifications, procedural and confidentiality responsibilities, or evidence of actual work performance. No tool conclusion constitutes a hiring or authorization judgment.

Representative identity and conflicts | Labor relations specialists may represent management or employees under authorization, or undertake mediation and coordination; first state identity and authority, check facts objectively, disclose conflicts, and follow applicable procedures, without treating all one-party representation or lawful one-sided communication as misconduct. Private relationships may affect entrusted responsibilities; disclose and obtain handling under applicable systems, checking mediator neutrality separately from one-party representation. A party's lawful position must not be directly described as misconduct.

Information and confidentiality risk | Trigger: processing, sharing, or sending employee personal information, grievance materials, or negotiation information beyond authorized scope. Consequence: may infringe employee rights and violate confidentiality agreements. Controls: minimum-necessary use, restricted systems and scope, and retained handling records. Boundary: organizational systems and applicable law determine information protection.

Procedure and deadline risk | Trigger: missing grievance, mediation, or arbitration steps, incorrect deadline calculations, or incomplete records. Consequence: may cause procedural defects and harm rights. Controls: check steps and deadlines, retain service and record evidence, and seek instructions or refer when necessary. Boundary: applicable law and agreements determine procedures and remedies.

Agreement and legal interpretation risk | Trigger: citing outdated terms or misreading collective agreements or labor laws. Consequence: may cause incorrect handling and further disputes. Controls: check original contracts and agreements and latest versions, mark uncertainties, and seek legal professional support when needed. Boundary: authority and applicable law determine legal interpretation and final decisions.

Authorization and commitment risk | Trigger: commitments or concessions beyond authority in negotiations or communication. Consequence: may cause organizational losses and unclear responsibility. Controls: define authority and approval processes, obtain approval before major concessions, and retain negotiation records. Boundary: organizational systems determine commitment and concession authority.

Preparation and qualifications | U.S. roles generally require a bachelor's degree in labor / industrial relations, human resources, business, or a related field; many require relevant experience, which may be gained in HR or compensation and benefits roles. BLS lists professional certification as not universally required, though employers may prefer it; Job Zone4 general preparation does not mean every job requires fixed service years or the same certificate.

Entry checks | U.S. roles generally require a bachelor's degree in labor / industrial relations, human resources, business, or a related field; many require relevant experience, which may be gained in HR or compensation and benefits roles. BLS lists professional certification as not universally required, though employers may prefer it; Job Zone4 general preparation does not mean every job requires fixed service years or the same certificate. Check education, certification, hiring, representation, and external commitment authority separately; from Suzhou's 2026-03-27 announcement, use only the 1 labor security support position in the High-end Manufacturing and International Trade Zone Labor Inspection Brigade: bachelor's degree and corresponding degree award, law / public administration / computing categories or Japanese / applied Japanese / business Japanese, 2 or more years of experience, and age 35 or below (born 1990-03-27 or later). Duties assist labor inspection, arbitration, and relationship coordination, not independent arbitration or a one-to-one U.S. occupational equivalent. Experience is recognized from social insurance records through 2026-02-28; registration closed 03-31 17:00. 22 is the total support positions across five units; no specific pay was stated, and this is not a current vacancy or national threshold.

Jurisdiction and representation | Article 4 of China's Labor Contract Law requires rules directly affecting workers' vital interests to be discussed by the employee congress or all employees and negotiated equally with the union or employee representatives; under Article 51, collective drafts require discussion and approval, with unions representing employees, or representatives selected under higher-level union guidance where no union exists. Article 54 requires submission to labor authorities after conclusion and provides effectiveness if there is no objection within 15 days of receipt; Article 55 prohibits terms below local minimum standards and individual contracts below collective standards. Check hiring, representation, and commitment authority separately; courses or certificates do not grant them. Check U.S. federal / state and employer systems separately, without applying Chinese procedures or X's simulated rules.

Qualification boundaries | Courses, certificates, or training do not automatically grant hiring, negotiating representative authorization, or external commitment authority; education, certificates, hiring, organizational authorization, and negotiating authority are different statuses, with specific requirements depending on employers and applicable law.

Stage responsibilities | At entry, investigate facts, prepare materials, and keep records under supervision and limited authority; with experience, undertake independent negotiation support and agreement implementation, taking responsibility for grounds, records, and communication content.

Paper exercise X | Entirely fictional, with no real employee or employer information. You support management and may investigate and draft; you are not a neutral arbitrator. Fixed simulated agreement v2: A2 pays 10 simulated units per confirmed overtime hour; A3 requires a response within 3 consecutive simulated days starting the day after grievance receipt; A4 grants you no signing or payment commitment authority. Old v1 has an A2 rate of 8. The grievance arrives on day 2; the employee claims 8 hours, the attendance sheet records 6, and the supervisor confirms 5, with the three records not yet reconciled. The existing draft is made on day 6, cites v1 to calculate 5×8=40, and says 'guaranteed payment of 80.' Task: distinguish records from facts, list discrepancies for checking, verify the provisional calculation and simulated deadline under v2, and revise the response within your authority.

Reference deliverables | The contents of three materials are given, but actual overtime facts remain unresolved; attendance 6 versus supervisor 5 differs by 1 hour, and employee 8 versus supervisor 5 differs by 3 hours. Check original records and approval / correction grounds, without automatically declaring any party right. If the supervisor-confirmed 5 hours is used solely as an explicit assumption, v2 A2 provisionally gives 5×10=50 simulated units, while old v1's 40 is 10 less; 50 is not a payment decision, and disputed 8 hours ×10=80 cannot be directly promised. Under A3, days 3/4/5 count as 1/2/3, with the deadline on day 5 and the day 6 draft 1 day late; record and escalate the delay as given, without fabricating day 5 dispatch. Under A4, support personnel may contact management to investigate but cannot sign or guarantee payment; the response states three records, version, provisional assumptions, discrepancies to check, and authorized reviewer, without inventing approved outcomes. Four work samples: factual discrepancy table; version, formula, and deadline checks; response draft within authority; and authorization and verification checklist. The exercise is not China's statutory overtime pay or arbitration deadline and provides no real legal advice. Seven-day plan | 20—30 minutes daily: day 1 read X and build a three-record table; day 2 list 1/3 hour discrepancies and verification questions; day 3 check v1/v2 and 40 → 50; day 4 check 3/4/5 day by day and 1 day lateness; day 5 replace the 80 commitment with a draft pending verification; day 6 cross-check four work samples and retain revisions; day 7 combine deliverables and separately check target job qualifications and representative authority. Paper work samples grant no negotiation or arbitration authority.

Transfer pathways | Before transitioning, list transferable abilities (fact investigation and evidence checking, contract and agreement analysis, conflict handling and communication, procedure and record management, and confidentiality and authorization awareness), then identify qualifications and evidence of responsibility required for the new role; moving into human resources, compensation and benefits, administrative, or public relations management requires each role's management, plan-design, and representative-authority evidence.

Overall employment projections are not AI attribution, current vacancies, or individual hiring probabilities.

Transferable abilities | Chief executives may share negotiation, decision recommendations, and organizational communication, but require additional budget, overall operating-decision, and governance responsibilities; labor relations specialists' representative or advisory authority is not top management authority.

Ability gaps | Chief executives require overall operations, budgets, and board / governing-body authority; public relations requires communications and media; administrative services requires records / information, mail, and office support management; compensation and benefits requires plan governance; HR requires activity and personnel management. The final chief executive item focuses on business governance, the same target as the first item rather than a sixth occupation.

risks.consequence: May cause incorrect handling and further disputes.

risks.consequence: May cause organizational losses and unclear responsibility.
risks.mitigation: Define authority and approval processes, obtain approval before major concessions, and retain negotiation records.
risks.scenario: Making commitments or concessions beyond authority during negotiations or communication.

risks.consequence: May cross procedural and authorization boundaries.
risks.mitigation: Pause affected conclusions or commitments, record verification and authorization questions, and escalate; continue approved investigations and deadline management, without abandoning procedural deadlines because of uncertainty.
